findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Bank Rate to remain at 3.75% through 2026, falling to 3.25% by spring 2028
findings.detail: Monetary Policy Committee held Bank Rate at 3.75% at both Q1 meetings (30 April and 18 June 2026). MUFG treasury advisors forecast rates to remain on hold through 2026, with next reductions beginning H2 2027, reaching 3.25% by spring 2028, contingent on Consumer Price Index inflation peaking around 3.6%.
findings.matters: Interest rate forecast directly affects GMCA's refinancing strategy and future borrowing costs; peer councils rely on this context for their own borrowing decisions and market timing.
findings.figures: Bank Rate held at 3.75%; PWLB rates at 30 June 2026: 1-year 4.77%, 5-year 5.07%, 10-year 5.55%, 25-year 6.17%; forecast Bank Rate 3.5% by end 2027, 3.25% by spring 2028
findings.quote: We forecast the next reduction in Bank Rate to be made in H2 2027, with Bank Rate falling to a low of 3.25% by the start of 2028.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Authority achieved 4.04% average investment yield, outperforming SONIA by 31 basis points, on track for £9.67m budgeted return
findings.detail: With average funds of £473.7m invested across banks, councils, and money market funds, the authority exceeded Sterling Overnight Index Average returns through active treasury management. Budgeted investment return for 2026/27 of £9.67m is currently forecast to be achieved.
findings.matters: Investment income is material cash generator for the authority; outperformance against SONIA demonstrates effective treasury management and supports cash position.
findings.figures: Average investment rate 4.04% versus SONIA 3.73%; outperformance 0.31bps; budgeted return £9.670m; average funds invested £473.7m
findings.quote: The Authority achieved an average rate of 4.04% which outperformed the average backward looking Sterling Overnight Index Average (SONIA) rate by 0.31 bps. The Authority's budgeted investment return for 2026/27 is £9.670m, and we are currently forecast to achieve this.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Gross external debt forecast at £1,574.4m, £182.9m below budget; net borrowing declining
findings.detail: Both gross external debt and net borrowing are declining from budgeted levels. Gross debt forecast at £1,574.4m versus budget of £1,757.3m, and net borrowing at £1,518.4m versus budget of £1,707.3m. Ratio of financing costs to net revenue stream improving to 6.9% from budgeted 7.6%.
findings.matters: Falling debt across the balance sheet improves credit metrics and reduces refinancing volumes, positive signal to lenders on credit trajectory and debt serviceability.
findings.figures: Gross external debt £1,574.381m (budget £1,757.263m); Net borrowing £1,518.381m (budget £1,707.263m); Ratio of financing costs to net revenue stream 6.9% (budget 7.6%)
findings.quote: Gross external debt as at 31 March £1,757.263m £1,574.381m; Net borrowing as at 31 March £1,707.263m £1,518.381m

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Capital Financing Requirement forecast at £2,688.3m, £305.7m below budget
findings.detail: The Capital Financing Requirement is forecast to fall from budgeted £2,994.0m to £2,688.3m, with annual change in CFR £182.3m against budgeted £453.3m, and in-year borrowing requirement £370.0m against budgeted £567.0m. The paper does not explain whether this represents slippage in capital delivery, deferral of planned projects, or efficiency improvements.
findings.matters: A 10% reduction in planned capital investment affects both immediate borrowing need and the multi-year capital programme outlook; peer councils monitoring how others manage capital programmes in the current market, and lenders assessing whether deferral indicates financial constraint or prudent timing.
findings.figures: Capital expenditure £994.747m (budget £1,148.913m); Capital Financing Requirement £2,688.288m (budget £2,994.019m); Annual change in CFR £182.271m (budget £453.281m); In year borrowing requirement £370.000m (budget £566.956m)
findings.quote: Prudential Indicators 2025/26 Budget 2026/27 Forecast Capital expenditure £1,148.913m £994.747m Capital Financing Requirement (CFR) £2,994.019m £2,688.288m

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Opinion GMCA 2025-26 v1.2 Final
findings.headline: £72m of grant funding certified as spent in accordance with grant conditions
findings.detail: All 11 grant certifications in 2025/26 received positive assurance, covering £72.055m, confirming compliant spend on Local Energy Advice Demonstrators, Growth Hub, SHDF, 5G Innovations, Brownfield Housing Fund, Net Zero programmes and Made Smarter grants.
findings.matters: Demonstrates compliance with grant conditions, which protects the council from grant clawback or restrictions on future funding.
findings.figures: £72.055m total across 11 grants; all positive assurance
findings.quote: All grant certification work in 2025/26 received positive assurance, confirming that £72m of grant funding was spent in accordance with the relevant grant conditions.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Opinion GMCA 2025-26 v1.2 Final
findings.headline: Data breach incidents increased to 66 in 2025/26, including 7 still under investigation
findings.detail: 66 data breach incidents were reported in 2025/26, including 7 still under investigation. The report explicitly notes this is an increase compared with previous years. Incidents are reported to the GMCA SIDGI panel chaired by the Group CFO.
findings.matters: Increasing data breach incidents indicate weaknesses in data security controls and create compliance and reputational risk, while unresolved investigations represent ongoing exposure.
findings.figures: 66 incidents in 2025/26; 7 under investigation; increase from prior years
findings.quote: In 2025/26, 66 incidents were reported, including seven still under investigation. This is an increase compared with previous years.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Opinion GMCA 2025-26 v1.2 Final
findings.headline: Group Statement of Accounts published 10 July 2026, 10 days after statutory deadline
findings.detail: While GMCA's Single Entity Statement of Accounts was published on time, the Group Statement of Accounts was delayed to 10 July 2026 due to incomplete financial information from group entities. This follows a disclaimed opinion on 2024/25 financial statements and an ongoing lessons-learned exercise.
findings.matters: Late publication delays visibility of the full financial position to audit committee, members and lenders, and indicates coordination issues between group entities.
findings.figures: Published 10 July 2026 (deadline 30 June 2026)
findings.quote: GMCA published its draft Single Entity Statement of Accounts but was unable to publish the full Group Statement of Accounts by the statutory deadline of 30 June 2026 because financial information from group entities was incomplete. GMCA Finance worked with those entities to finalise the outstanding information, and the Group accounts were published on 10 July 2026.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Opinion GMCA 2025-26 v1.2 Final
findings.headline: Audit action implementation fell to 75% in March 2026, below 85% target and prior year
findings.detail: Implementation of agreed audit actions fell below the 85% target during 2025/26, reaching only 75% by March 2026, declining from above 85% in March 2025. The report attributes this to organisational capacity constraints. The chart shows the number of overdue and tracked actions has increased.
findings.matters: Low implementation rates mean control weaknesses identified by auditors are not being resolved, leaving identified risks unaddressed.
findings.figures: 75% implementation rate (March 2026); 85% target; prior year above 85%
findings.quote: Implementation of agreed audit actions fell below the 85% target during 2025/26, reaching 75% by March 2026. Further management focus is required to ensure actions are completed on time.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Opinion GMCA 2025-26 v1.2 Final
findings.headline: Officer Declarations of Interest audit received No Assurance opinion with three high-risk findings
findings.detail: One of 12 internal audit reports received a No Assurance rating on Officer Declarations of Interest and Gifts and Hospitality (Officers), with 3 high-risk findings and 2 medium-risk findings. No Assurance is the lowest assurance level, indicating the control system is ineffective or absent.
findings.matters: Officers' declarations of interest are a fundamental control for preventing conflicts of interest in decision-making, and a No Assurance rating indicates this process is not effectively managing this risk.
findings.figures: 1 No Assurance report; 5 findings (3 high-risk, 2 medium-risk)
findings.quote: One no assurance report was issued on Officer Declarations of Interest, with action being taken to address the findings.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Government readiness assessment identified gaps in scarce skills including programme management, commercial/procurement, data, cyber and evaluation capabilities needed for delivery priorities
findings.detail: A readiness assessment noted that workforce planning needs a more strategic approach tied to delivery priorities. The authority commits to developing an integrated workforce plan tied to Integrated Settlement and wider portfolio delivery, with specific focus on ensuring coverage of programme management, commercial/procurement, data, cyber, and evaluation skills.
findings.matters: Workforce capability directly affects delivery of major programmes and risk management; gaps in critical skills like cyber and commercial capability create delivery and governance risk.
findings.figures: Identified scarce skills gaps: programme management, commercial/procurement, data, cyber, evaluation
findings.quote: The development of an integrated workforce plan tied to delivery priorities (Integrated Settlement and wider portfolio), and ensure scarce skills coverage (programme management, commercial / procurement, data, cyber, evaluation).

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Single Settlement and grant dependency identified as significant forward risk where funding assumption changes could create shortfalls and force programme re-scoping
findings.detail: The authority identifies that multi-year funding assumptions can change due to government policy decisions or spending review outcomes, creating shortfalls and requiring re-scoping of programmes. The Integrated Settlement is noted as a key dependency. Mitigations include medium-term financial planning, scenario testing, active management of grant conditions, and robust business case discipline.
findings.matters: Core risk for a body heavily reliant on government grant funding, particularly material given the Integrated Settlement as a major revenue stream.
findings.figures: Identified as principal forward-looking risk in risk register
findings.quote: Multi-year funding assumptions change (policy/spending review outcomes), creating shortfalls and forcing re-scoping of programmes.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Government readiness assessment identified limited multi-year forecasting outside transport programmes and variance in forecasting practice across the authority
findings.detail: A readiness assessment highlighted that multi-year financial forecasting is limited in most areas beyond transport, and practice varies across the organisation. The authority commits to developing multi-year forecasting across the full portfolio and standardising variable practice, aligned with outcomes and evaluation for the Integrated Settlement.
findings.matters: Multi-year forecasting is essential for assessing financial sustainability and planning delivery of major programmes; limited visibility creates uncertainty about future financial position and funding needs.
findings.figures: Limited multi-year forecasting identified outside transport programmes; variance in practice noted
findings.quote: The readiness assessment highlighted limited multi-year forecasting outside some transport programmes, and variance in practice in some areas.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Audit action implementation fell below 85% target, reaching 75% by March 2026, with limited assurance areas at only 61%
findings.detail: The organisation tracks implementation of agreed audit recommendations against an 85% target. Overall implementation reached 75% by March 2026, missing the target. For the three areas with limited assurance, implementation was lower at 61%, indicating that improvements in weak control areas are being addressed slower than planned.
findings.matters: Slow implementation of audit recommendations means identified control weaknesses persist longer and risk mitigation is delayed.
findings.figures: Overall: 75% actual vs 85% target; limited assurance areas: 61% actual vs 85% target
findings.quote: Audit action implementation fell below the 85% target, reaching 75% by March 2026

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Three core control areas received Limited Assurance opinions: Accounts Payable, overtime and on-call arrangements, and ICT/Digital asset management
findings.detail: Internal audit assigned Limited Assurance (indicating significant improvements required) to Accounts Payable controls, overtime and on-call arrangements for Green Book employees, and ICT/Digital asset management. Issues include weaknesses in segregation of duties and user access controls in Accounts Payable; absence of clear corporate policy on overtime/on-call creating inconsistent management; and gaps across asset lifecycle governance, disposal and automation.
findings.matters: These three areas span financial transactions, payroll governance, and asset management—fundamental control functions. Limited Assurance signals that medium and high-risk exceptions remain unresolved.
findings.figures: Three areas with Limited Assurance designation
findings.quote: The July 2026 Internal Audit Progress Report highlights three principal Limited Assurance areas: overtime and on-call arrangements for Green Book employees, Accounts Payable controls, and ICT/Digital asset management.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: External auditor issued disclaimer of opinion on 2024/25 accounts due to statutory publication backstop, with value-for-money recommendation on financial reporting and governance weaknesses
findings.detail: The auditor could not complete all required audit procedures by the statutory deadline, resulting in a disclaimer of opinion. The auditor also reported a value-for-money recommendation identifying significant weaknesses in financial reporting, audit-support arrangements, governance around the new ledger, budgetary control, and Audit Committee effectiveness.
findings.matters: A disclaimer is a qualification affecting audit opinion; the identified weaknesses in financial reporting and budgetary control go to the core of financial governance and accountability.
findings.figures: Disclaimer of opinion issued; value-for-money recommendation issued
findings.quote: the external auditor issued a disclaimer of opinion because of the national audit backstop deadline and reported a VfM recommendation due to a significant weakness in financial reporting and audit-support arrangements

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Transport services overspent £36m against a £410m budget in 2025/26
findings.detail: Transport expenditure exceeded the approved budget by £36m (8.8% overspend). The assessment identifies transport as presenting a 'Significant area of financial exposure', with risks centred on income, operating costs and service sustainability. Transport earmarked reserves are flagged with pressure noted.
findings.matters: Transport is GMCA's largest single service budget. An £36m overspend on top of flagged reserve pressure signals tighter operating margins and reduced resilience to manage future cost pressures.
findings.figures: £36m overspend; transport budget £410m approved, £447m outturn; transport reserves £172m assessed 'Adequate/pressure noted'

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Earmarked reserves drawn down by £53.3m to £462.6m; capital receipts reduced by £10.7m to fund activities in place of borrowing
findings.detail: The Authority used reserves and cash balances instead of raising debt, achieving gross borrowing reduction of £78.8m. However, this reduction was funded by drawing down reserves rather than service surpluses or receipt generation, raising questions about the sustainability of this position.
findings.matters: Reserve levels and trends are key indicators of financial resilience for lenders and peer councils. While debt reduction is positive, funding it through reserve depletion rather than improved operations suggests reliance on a finite buffer. The CFR closed at £2,506.0m (£34.3m above budget), indicating the underlying borrowing need remains substantial.
findings.figures: Earmarked reserves £462.626m vs prior year £515.931m (down £53.305m); usable capital receipts £178.287m vs £189.012m (down £10.725m); CFR closing £2,506.017m vs budget £2,471.749m
findings.quote: During 2025/26, the Authority maintained an under-borrowed position. This meant that the capital borrowing need, (the CFR), was not fully funded with loan debt as cash supporting the Authority's reserves, balances and cash flow was used as an interim measure.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Investment income reached £17.2m against budget of £2.3m—more than seven times planned—through active cash management at elevated short-term rates
findings.detail: The Authority achieved an average return of 4.19% on average internal funds of £410.6m, outperforming the Sterling Overnight Index Average (SONIA) benchmark of 4.01%. This substantially exceeded the conservative investment budget despite Bank Rate falling from 4.50% to 3.75% over the year.
findings.matters: This outcome illustrates the financial benefit of the under-borrowed strategy and demonstrates active cash management delivering material returns. For finance directors, it shows the value (and risk of losing) high short-term rates. The budget miss suggests investment assumptions were highly conservative or the Authority improved its deployment tactics.
findings.figures: Total investment income £17.2m vs budget £2.3m; average internal funds £410.6m; average return 4.19% vs SONIA 4.01%
findings.quote: Total investment income was £17.2m compared to a budget of £2.3m.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: No long-term borrowing undertaken during 2025/26 due to elevated PWLB rates, leaving future refinancing need unaddressed
findings.detail: The Authority deliberately maintained an under-borrowed position, using temporary borrowing and cash reserves instead. £100m temporary borrowing was arranged at year-end (Feb-Mar 2026) at 4.90–5.30%, maturing April 2026. This strategy reflected PWLB rates that spiked to 5.88% in late March 2026 following the Middle East conflict.
findings.matters: For lenders and peer councils, this shows the capital financing response to a prolonged high-rate environment. The deferred borrowing creates a future liability; whether it will be manageable depends on rate movements. It also demonstrates the marginal economics: internal cash returns of 4.19% were nearly competitive with borrowing costs above 5%.
findings.figures: No long-term borrowing undertaken 2025/26; temporary borrowing £100m at 4.90–5.30%; 10-year PWLB high 5.88% (27 March 2026), average 5.38%
findings.quote: Due to the elevated cost of borrowing, no long-term borrowing was undertaken during the year.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Capital expenditure delivered at £520.2m, £116.1m below budget of £636.3m, with financing in-year also falling short of plan
findings.detail: Actual capital spending came in significantly below budget. Financed in-year was £412.3m against budget £509.7m. This underspend, combined with lower unfinanced capital expenditure (£107.9m vs £126.6m budgeted), suggests either scheme deferrals or revised capital priorities.
findings.matters: Capital delivery variance of this scale is material to councils' borrowing need forecasts and capacity to deliver strategic programmes. For lenders, it affects the accuracy of CFR projections and future refinancing requirements. For peer councils, it's a benchmark for delivery tracking.
findings.figures: 2025/26 actual £520.198m vs budget £636.317m; financed in year £412.336m vs budget £509.671m; unfinanced £107.862m vs budget £126.646m
findings.quote: Capital expenditure 2025/26 Budget £m 636.317, 2025/26 Actual £m 520.198

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: 8. 20260309_TMSS, MRP Policy Statement and Annual Investment Strategy 202627
findings.headline: Interest rate forecasts carry multiple upside risks to borrowing costs
findings.detail: MUFG forecasts Bank Rate at 3.25% by Q4 2026, but identifies significant risks: wage growth remains above 4.5% annually; political uncertainty over whether the government will serve a full term; US monetary policy decisions; and inflation sticky near 3%. The treasury adviser explicitly states: the updated central forecast is made with several hefty caveats.
findings.matters: These forecasts underpin the authority's under-borrowing strategy; if risks materialise, borrowing costs could be significantly higher and the tactical position exposed.
findings.figures: Bank Rate forecast 3.75% (22 Dec 2025) to 3.25% (Q4 2026); annual wage growth 4.5%+; CPI inflation 3.2%.
findings.quote: the updated central forecast is made with several hefty caveats

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: 8. 20260309_TMSS, MRP Policy Statement and Annual Investment Strategy 202627
findings.headline: Investment earnings on cash balances forecast to fall from 3.80% to 3.40%
findings.detail: The expected decline in Bank Rate reduces the returns available on short-term treasury investments. This cuts the financial benefit of holding cash balances, reducing investment income available to support the revenue budget.
findings.matters: This is a real reduction in financial resources; it compounds the impact of declining rates by reducing income while the authority's borrowing costs also fall.
findings.figures: 2025/26 residual: 3.80%; 2026/27 forecast: 3.40%; decline of 40 basis points.
findings.quote: Average earnings in each year Now Previously 2025/26 (residual) 3.80% 3.90% 2026/27 3.40% 3.60%

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: 8. 20260309_TMSS, MRP Policy Statement and Annual Investment Strategy 202627
findings.headline: Financing costs rise to 9.7% of net revenue by 2028/29 from 7.6% in 2026/27
findings.detail: The ratio of debt service costs to revenue shows a rising trend over the forecast period. This reflects a growing stock of debt and rising interest costs, despite the forecast decline in borrowing rates. The rise indicates increasing pressure on future revenue budgets.
findings.matters: Growing financing costs crowd out spending on services; peers and lenders need to assess whether this trajectory is sustainable and what budget headroom remains.
findings.quote: Ratio of Financing Costs to Net Revenue Stream 8.5% 7.7% 7.6% 8.6% 9.7%

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: 8. 20260309_TMSS, MRP Policy Statement and Annual Investment Strategy 202627
findings.headline: Capital expenditure forecast at £1,148.913m in 2026/27, 87% higher than the preceding year
findings.detail: The 2026/27 capital programme is heavily concentrated in a single year, falling back to £629.745m in 2027/28. Economic Development & Regeneration accounts for £652.484m of the spike (2025/26: £238.282m), more than doubling year-on-year.
findings.matters: Lenders need to assess delivery risk and cash flow impact of such a concentrated programme; peer councils would want to understand how this is being financed and managed.
findings.figures: 2025/26 capital expenditure £612.240m; 2026/27 £1,148.913m; Economic Development & Regeneration 2025/26 £238.282m, 2026/27 £652.484m.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: GMCA confirms no investments undertaken solely for commercial yield purposes, positioning against PWLB access restrictions
findings.detail: Group Chief Financial Officer declares the capital programme contains no speculative commercial investments, reflecting Government policy discouraging such activity through PWLB access controls. Any future commercial investment would require full GMCA approval and acknowledgement of financing risk implications.
findings.matters: Signals compliance with Government borrowing policy and awareness of PWLB access restrictions; indicates disciplined risk stance compared to councils that pursued commercial yield strategies before policy tightening
findings.figures: None
findings.quote: As such the Group Chief Financial Officer declares that the Authority plans for capital investment as outlined in the capital programme do not contain any investments solely for commercial yield purposes.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Greater Manchester Housing Investment Fund closed March 2025; MHCLG announced recapitalisation and extension in Spending Review
findings.detail: The original HIF closed for new commitments in March 2025 after supporting delivery of over 11,000 homes. MHCLG announced recapitalisation and extension, with future deployment managed within Good Growth Fund monies, ensuring continuity of the housing investment vehicle rather than replacement.
findings.matters: Housing investment programme continues under new structure; signals sustained central government backing for housing; consolidates into integrated strategy rather than establishing new dedicated vehicle
findings.figures: 11,000+ homes delivered by original HIF; original fund repayment due 2028
findings.quote: MHCLG announced the recapitalisation of the Fund and extension in the Spending Review – future deployment of the Fund will be managed within the overall Good Growth Fund monies.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Good Growth Fund launched with £150m GMCA borrowing and £300m Greater Manchester Pension Fund commitment
findings.detail: November 2025 approval of the Good Growth Fund combines Integrated settlement monies, £150m new GMCA borrowing, and £300m Greater Manchester Pension Fund investment to fund housing, employment, town centre regeneration, transport and innovation. The fund will blend flexible grant funding with recycled money to maximise pipeline impact.
findings.matters: Material new funding vehicle linking public authority and pension fund capital; the £150m borrowing is a significant component of the 2026/27 borrowing spike; demonstrates blended financing approach to priority regeneration
findings.figures: £150m GMCA borrowing; £300m Greater Manchester Pension Fund commitment
findings.quote: In order to kickstart investment into the pipeline, the launch of the Good Growth Fund was announced, utilising out Integrated settlement monies alongside £150m borrowing and a commitment from the Greater Manchester Pension Fund to invest £300m into the pipeline.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: External debt forecast to rise from £1.401bn to £1.758bn by 2028/29, with borrowing limits expanding in line
findings.detail: Closing external debt for 2025/26 is forecast at £1.401bn (including PFI liabilities), rising to £1.758bn by end 2028/29. The Authorised Limit increases to £3,317.366m for 2026/27 from £2,823.455m in 2025/26, reflecting the rising capital programme. The authority uses internal borrowing (cash surpluses) to manage debt but the underlying debt trajectory is upward.
findings.matters: Rising absolute debt and expanding borrowing limits signal increasing leverage; lenders assess medium-term debt sustainability and refinancing risk as absolute debt grows by £357m over the forecast period
findings.quote: At the end of 2025/26 it is forecast that the GMCA's external debt will be £1.401 billion (including PFI liabilities) and this is forecast to be £1.758 billion by the end of 2028/29.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Borrowing requirement increases 299% to £566.956m in 2026/27, financing nearly half the capital programme
findings.detail: The authority's borrowing need jumps from £142.175m in 2025/26 to £566.956m in 2026/27, representing 49.3% of that year's capital programme. This is part of planned prudential borrowing of £998m across 2025/26–2028/29, including the £150m new borrowing for the Good Growth Fund announced November 2025.
findings.matters: A near-300% increase in annual borrowing creates material interest cost and debt servicing exposure; demonstrates heavy reliance on borrowed funds rather than grants or capital receipts for 2026/27
findings.figures: 2026/27 borrowing £566.956m vs 2025/26 £142.175m; total prudential borrowing 2025/26–2028/29 £998m; Good Growth Fund borrowing £150m
findings.quote: The capital programme is reliant on prudential borrowing totalling £ 998m between 2025/26 and 2028/29.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Capital expenditure forecast to rise 88% to £1.149bn in 2026/27, driven by Economic Development jumping 174%, before falling back sharply
findings.detail: The 2026/27 capital programme reaches £1,148.913m, largely driven by Economic Development and Regeneration rising to £652.484m from £238.282m in 2025/26 – primarily social housing decarbonisation and regeneration schemes funded through borrowing and the Good Growth Fund. The programme then reduces to £629.745m in 2027/28, creating a concentrated expenditure profile.
findings.matters: A single year carrying a peak spike in activity signals potential delivery and cash-flow concentration risk; the jump in one service area may strain implementation capacity and complicate refinancing

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Internal audit reports shift to more limited and no assurance opinions; high-risk agreed actions increased from 4 to 12
findings.detail: Compared to 2023/24, the 2024/25 internal audit work shows deterioration in the pattern of assurance opinions (shift from 2 substantial/6 reasonable in 2023/24 to 0 substantial/5 reasonable in 2024/25, with increases in limited and no assurance ratings) and an increase in the proportion of high-risk agreed audit actions requiring management attention.
findings.matters: A shift towards lower assurance opinions and more high-risk findings suggests the control environment may be weakening and that previously identified issues may not have been adequately resolved.
findings.figures: 2024/25: 1 no assurance opinion, 5 limited, 5 reasonable; 2023/24: 0 no assurance, 2 limited, 6 reasonable. High-risk actions: 12 vs 4 prior year
findings.quote: shift from 2023/24 to a greater proportion of limited and no assurance opinions. There has also been shift in the composition of agreed actions, from advisory and low to medium and high risk

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Breakeven 2024/25 revenue outturn achieved only through drawdown of £8.4m from reserves, above the £7.2m budget
findings.detail: While the headline position was breakeven, this masked an underlying deficit that had to be covered by above-budget reserve drawdowns. Income and expenditure both exceeded budget by approximately £50m, driven by additional grant funding and business rate retention, but this additional activity and income did not prevent the reserve draw exceeding plan.
findings.matters: The underlying position is weaker than the headline breakeven suggests; sustainable financial management requires the organisation to operate closer to funding without relying on incremental drawdowns.
findings.figures: Reserves drawn: £8.4m; Budgeted: £7.2m; Total income and expenditure both ~£50m above budget
findings.quote: In achieving this breakeven position, a total of £8.4m was drawn from total group reserves, above the initially budgeted £7.2m use of reserves

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Transport for Greater Manchester identified £16m efficiency requirements for 2025/26; Greater Manchester Police £19m
findings.detail: Major service areas are facing significant cost-saving targets. Actions to deliver these include recruitment scrutiny and pauses, expenditure scrutiny panels, and work to identify additional income sources. These are recurrent efficiency pressures, not one-off savings.
findings.matters: Large efficiency requirements in major service areas signal financial pressure and carry risk of service delivery impact; a lender needs to understand whether these savings are deliverable without affecting service resilience.
findings.figures: TfGM £16m; GMP £19m
findings.quote: Transport for Greater Manchester and Policing budgets for 2025/26 identify efficiency requirements of approximately £16m and £19m respectively

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Total usable reserves fell from 65% of annual expenditure to 52%, with £8.4m drawn down in 2024/25 against budgeted £7.2m
findings.detail: The auditor notes explicitly that this level of planned reserve drawings is not sustainable. Reserves have been declining year-on-year, largely through planned drawdowns to support transport transformation. While current reserve levels are described as appropriate, the trajectory and sustainability of these drawdowns are a concern.
findings.matters: Declining reserves reduce financial headroom to absorb shocks or fund unexpected pressures; a lender will want to understand whether the drawdown rate is sustainable or whether future financial pressures will force unsustainable further depletion.
findings.figures: 2024/25: 52% of annual expenditure; 2023/24: 65% of annual expenditure; £8.4m drawn (£7.2m budgeted)
findings.quote: This level of planned drawings is not sustainable but has been undergoing organisational change in relation to transport requiring planned reserve draw downs

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Significant weakness in governance: finance team resourcing and accounts closedown planning inadequate to meet statutory reporting timelines
findings.detail: The auditor identified that GMCA failed to plan sufficient time for the transition to IFRS16 and experienced unplanned staff absences during critical phases, creating single points of failure in the finance team. The auditor recommends reviewing the capacity and capability of the group finance team and the accounts closedown plan to ensure statutory deadlines are met in future.
findings.matters: A lender needs assurance that the authority has the financial management capacity to maintain accurate, timely reporting and meet compliance obligations.
findings.figures: Work on IFRS16 transition began late 2022 for land and property, but vehicle and equipment leasing work started later than planned
findings.quote: Resourcing constraints and failure to plan sufficient time to support preparation for transition to the new standard represents a significant weakness in these arrangements

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Auditor concluded value-for-money arrangements are not appropriate to secure economy, efficiency and effectiveness
findings.detail: The auditor issued an adverse VFM conclusion due to a significant weakness in governance: GMCA's processes and systems do not support the delivery of statutory financial reporting within the required deadlines. This is the formal audit finding triggering the modified conclusion.
findings.matters: An adverse VFM conclusion signals to lenders that the authority has not maintained adequate internal controls or financial management systems to meet its statutory obligations.
findings.figures: VFM conclusion: not satisfied
findings.quote: we are not satisfied that GMCA's arrangements in relation to governance are appropriate to secure value for money

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Statement of Accounts published 7 October 2025, three months after the statutory 30 June 2025 deadline
findings.detail: Publication was delayed because GMCA and its component entities, particularly Transport for Greater Manchester, encountered significant difficulties implementing IFRS16 (the new leases accounting standard) despite this being planned for several years. The delays were compounded by unplanned staff absences and resourcing challenges in the finance team.
findings.matters: Statutory reporting delays indicate governance and financial control weaknesses; they also compress the audit timeline and create risk of material errors going undetected.
findings.figures: Statutory deadline: 30 June 2025; Actual publication: 7 October 2025
findings.quote: publication of the Statement of Accounts was delayed until 7th October 2025

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Auditor disclaimed opinion on financial statements due to insufficient time to complete audit procedures
findings.detail: The auditor was unable to form an opinion on whether the 2024/25 financial statements present a true and fair view, citing the backstop deadline of 27 February 2026 and delays in completing audit work caused by the delayed publication of the accounts. This is the most serious audit outcome, leaving users with no assurance over the financial position.
findings.matters: A lender cannot rely on audited financial statements to assess the authority's financial position, borrowing capacity, or covenant compliance.
findings.figures: Opinion disclaimed on 24 February 2026
findings.quote: Our opinion on the financial statements is disclaimed due to there being insufficient time to complete our audit procedures ahead of the 27th February backstop deadline.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: No fraud, non-compliance with law, or significant internal control deficiencies identified at GMCA
findings.detail: Auditors report awaiting final responses from management on fraud and compliance matters but to date have no matters to report in these areas. No significant deficiencies in internal control have been identified, and no other control observations requiring attention are reported.
findings.matters: In context of a disclaimed opinion and material unadjusted misstatements at TfGM, the absence of detected fraud or control failures at GMCA provides limited additional assurance on governance integrity, though it does not substitute for missing audit assurance on financial statements.
findings.figures: No material misstatements identified and corrected above reporting threshold
findings.quote: but to date, have no matters to report in relation to fraud and the Authority's compliance with laws and regulations.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Management undertaking finance team resourcing review and accounts closedown process improvements to address governance weakness
findings.detail: In response to the identified governance weakness, GMCA is reviewing finance team resourcing across the group to provide additional support to accounts preparation, and reviewing the accounts closedown plan to identify efficiencies and ensure project milestones support statutory deadline compliance with high-quality supporting papers.
findings.matters: Management's commitment to remediate the identified weakness is critical context for assessing whether the organisation can restore timely reporting. Lenders and peer finance directors would track whether these actions successfully prevent recurrence in future reporting cycles.
findings.figures: Scale audit fee 2024/25: £257,585; total audit fee charged: £140,793 (up from £113,688 in 2023/24)
findings.quote: GMCA are undertaking a review of resourcing across the finance team to provide additional support to the Statement of Accounts preparation process in future years. A review of the accounts preparation process is taking place, with a view to identifying further efficiencies in the closedown process

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Significant governance weakness identified: GMCA missed June 2025 draft accounts deadline due to incomplete IFRS16 implementation planning
findings.detail: Auditors identified a significant weakness in GMCA's governance arrangements for statutory financial reporting. GMCA and the group failed to publish draft Statement of Accounts by the 30 June 2025 statutory deadline because IFRS16 (leases) implementation work was not complete. Despite IFRS16 being planned for years with material impact anticipated, no adequate plan was established for identifying affected leases and calculating entries within the closedown timeframe.
findings.matters: Failure to meet statutory deadlines for draft accounts signals inadequate capacity, planning discipline, or resource management in the finance function. This cascades into delays affecting final publication and audit completion, and is material to peers assessing how others manage reporting pressures.
findings.figures: Statutory deadline for draft accounts: 30 June 2025; final audited publication deadline: 28 February 2026
findings.quote: GMCA and the GMCA group was unable to publish its draft Statement of Accounts for the year ending 31 March 2025 by the statutory deadline of 30th June due to work in relation to the implementation of the accounting standard 'IFRS16 – leases' not being complete.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Material unadjusted misstatements in TfGM financial statements affecting GMCA group accounts remain unresolved
findings.detail: TfGM (Transport for Greater Manchester), a significant component audited by Forvis Mazars (covering 99% of group expenditure), has multiple areas of material misstatement unresolved: right of use assets and PPE not valued on appropriate basis; assets under construction improperly capitalized; operating lease commitments misstated due to IFRS16 transition failures; and IFRS16 lease liability calculation errors. GMCA cannot adjust group accounts because TfGM has not completed necessary work.
findings.matters: Unadjusted material misstatements in asset valuations and lease accounting prevent the group accounts from presenting a true and fair view of financial position. This directly affects lenders' credit assessment and peer finance directors' understanding of financial health.
findings.figures: TfGM audited component materiality calculated separately; auditor covers 99% of group expenditure
findings.quote: If appropriate valuations cannot be obtained by the backstop deadline, the GMCA disclaimed opinion may require modification to outline this 'other matter' that may have a material impact on the group financial statements.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Auditors will disclaim opinion on 2024/25 financial statements due to insufficient audit procedures before statutory publication deadline
findings.detail: The auditors intend to issue a disclaimer of opinion on GMCA's financial statements because the statutory backstop arrangements (requiring publication by 28 February 2026) did not allow sufficient time to complete all required audit procedures. The effect of the lack of evidence is material and pervasive. A disclaimer means no assurance is provided on whether the financial statements present a true and fair view.
findings.matters: A disclaimed opinion removes all audit assurance on the financial statements, which lenders and peer finance directors rely on to assess financial reliability. This is a fundamental impairment of the audit function and affects creditworthiness assessment.
findings.figures: Overall materiality group: £54.6m (2024/25) vs £46.9m (2023/24). Publication deadline: 28 February 2026.
findings.quote: As a result, we intend to issue a disclaimer of opinion on the Authority's financial statements.

findings.committee: AGMA Executive Board
findings.headline: 2025/26 forecast outturn shows £165k underspend on Resilience Unit, offset by reduced reserve usage to achieve breakeven position
findings.detail: The GM Resilience Network is forecast to underspend by £165k against a budget of £1.033m. Budgeted reserve draws from Resilience Unit Reserves were £185k; actual draws forecast at £20k, meaning the underspend offset reserve usage and delivered a net breakeven position without additional pressure on general reserves.
findings.matters: Shows in-year financial management discipline and forecast accuracy; peers monitor whether authorities recover underspends and manage reserve draws effectively
findings.figures: £165k underspend on Resilience Unit; budgeted reserve drawdown £185k, forecast actual drawdown £20k
findings.quote: The forecast outturn position for the year ending 31 March 2026 is forecasting a £165k underspend on the Resilience Unit, which will be offset by reduced reserve usage to show a breakeven position.

findings.committee: AGMA Executive Board
findings.headline: District contributions to AGMA reduced by £80k to £1.452m in 2026/27 despite 3% pay award applied to staffing
findings.detail: District contributions fall from £1.532m in 2025/26 to £1.452m in 2026/27. This reduction is achieved while applying a 3% pay award to retained staff within AGMA, indicating that cost increases are offset by service externalisations. Individual council contributions are set out in Appendix 1.
findings.matters: Finance directors monitor the cost of shared services; a reduction in contributions despite inflation signals cost management and affects each council's own budget envelope
findings.figures: District contributions 2025/26: £1.532m; 2026/27: £1.452m; reduction of £80k; 3% pay award applied
findings.quote: This reflects two functions (the Waste and Minerals Unit and Flood and Water Management) being funded by GMCA from 2026/27 and an increase in line with the Green Book pay award (3 %) to provide sufficient funding for the other functions.

findings.committee: AGMA Executive Board
findings.headline: Waste and Minerals Unit and Flood and Water Management funding transferred to GMCA from 2026/27; Archaeology and Ecology services transitioning to external Service Level Agreements during 2026/27
findings.detail: Following November 2025 decisions, Waste and Minerals Unit (£64k) and 50% of Flood and Water Management funding (£37k) transfer to GMCA funding. Archaeology Service (£156k budgeted for 2026/27) and Ecology Unit (£229k budgeted for 2026/27) are transitioning to Service Level Agreement arrangements outside AGMA's direct control. These changes remove £486k of service costs from AGMA's direct funding responsibility.
findings.matters: The restructuring of service delivery and funding models is relevant for finance directors at other councils tracking how joint arrangements evolve and considering implications for their own shared services
findings.figures: Waste and Minerals Unit £64k to GMCA, Flood and Water Management £37k (50%) to GMCA, Archaeology Service £156k (to SLA), Ecology Unit £229k (to SLA)
findings.quote: Following a report to AGMA in November 2025 it was agreed that from 2026/27 GMCA will fund the waste and minerals unit... Following a report to AGMA in November 2025 it was agreed that from 2026/27 GMCA will fund the 50% of the post previously funded by LA's.

findings.committee: AGMA Executive Board
findings.headline: AGMA general reserves forecast to decline from £138k (6% of budget) at March 2025 to £98k (4% of budget) at March 2027
findings.detail: General reserves are on a declining trajectory: £138k at 31 March 2025 declining to £118k (5% of budget) at 31 March 2026, with further decline to £98k (4% of budget) forecast for 31 March 2027. The authority previously returned £350k to districts at March 2025. The declining reserves percentage indicates tightening financial flexibility.
findings.matters: Finance directors and lenders monitor reserve adequacy as a resilience measure; a progressive decline signals reduced financial buffering and may indicate underlying pressures in AGMA's service sustainability
findings.figures: £138k at 31 March 2025 (6% of budget), £118k at 31 March 2026 (5% of budget), £98k projected at 31 March 2027 (4% of budget); £350k previously returned to districts
findings.quote: The position on General AGMA reserves at 31st March 2025 was £138k after returning £350k back to the districts. The forecast balance for 31st March 2026 is £118k which represents 5% of the AGMA proposed budget for 2026/27.
